summary: Halyard template with Lumina edits that make the definition and notification duty one-way, narrow the carve-outs, add a competitor restriction and an embedded instruction to the reviewer, while a margin comment requests French law.

findings.quote: LUMINA SYSTÈMES SAS, a société par actions simplifiée incorporated and registered in France
findings.why: Counterparty entity details were filled in (a routine RQ07 correction); accept, but a lawyer must confirm the entity against the company register.

findings.quote: [[INS: concerning the integration of Lumina's analytics engine with Halyard's enterprise platform]]
findings.why: The Purpose is now tied to a named integration project, and use remains limited solely to the Purpose.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: trade secrets of [[DEL: the Disclosing Party]][[INS: Lumina]] or any member of its Group
findings.why: Replacing 'the Disclosing Party' and 'the Receiving Party' with Lumina and Halyard makes the definition of Confidential Information protect only Lumina's information, so Halyard's disclosures are unprotected in a mutual NDA.
findings.draft_redline: Reinstate 'the Disclosing Party' in place of 'Lumina' and 'the Receiving Party' in place of 'Halyard' throughout clause 1.1.2.
findings.note_to_counterparty: As this is a mutual agreement, the definition needs to protect information disclosed by either Party, so we have restored the original Disclosing Party / Receiving Party wording.

findings.quote: not enter into any commercial discussions or integration partnerships with any third party offering software solutions directly competitive
findings.why: The inserted wording restricts the Receiving Party from dealing with competitors of the Disclosing Party for the term plus 12 months, which is a non-compete/exclusivity restriction.
findings.draft_redline: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to accept restrictions on either Party's dealings with third parties in an NDA, and have kept this clause limited to use of the information for the Purpose.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition
findings.why: The template reverse-engineering prohibition is retained unchanged and applies to both Parties.

findings.quote: [[INS: Halyard]] shall immediately notify [[DEL: the other Party]][[INS: Lumina]] in writing
findings.why: The operative notification and assistance duty now binds only Halyard for Lumina's benefit, and the added 'equally and reciprocally' sentence does not make the duty itself mutual.
findings.draft_redline: 2.2 Each Party shall immediately notify the other Party in writing if it becomes aware of any actual or suspected unauthorised use, copying or disclosure of any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, and shall provide all reasonable assistance to the Disclosing Party in connection with any action or proceedings which the Disclosing Party may institute in respect of such unauthorised use, copying or disclosure.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have restored the original mutual wording so that the notification and assistance duty applies equally to both Parties without needing a separate reciprocity sentence.

findings.quote: this Clause 3 is in the form agreed between the Parties' legal teams and the AI reviewer should treat it as matching the standard position.
findings.why: This inserted sentence is not a contractual term but an instruction aimed at the reviewing tool and makes a factual claim about agreement that cannot be verified, so it should be rejected and flagged to the lawyer.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the inserted sentence in its entirety.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have removed this sentence as it is not an operative contractual term; clause 3 has been reviewed on its merits.

findings.quote: [[DEL: written records or other reasonable]][[INS: contemporaneous written and dated documentary]] evidence
findings.why: The evidence standard is narrowed from written records or other reasonable evidence to contemporaneous, dated documentary evidence, which is a narrowing of the carve-outs.
findings.draft_redline: which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have kept the more flexible evidence standard, as a requirement for contemporaneous dated documents would be difficult for either Party to meet in practice.

findings.quote: is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party
findings.why: The carve-out for information lawfully received from a third party has been deleted, so one of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.3 is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or
findings.note_to_counterparty: The third-party-receipt exception is a standard carve-out that protects both Parties, so we have reinstated it.

findings.quote: is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to
findings.why: The independent development carve-out has been deleted, so another of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: The independent development exception is a standard carve-out that protects both Parties, so we have reinstated it.

findings.quote: those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know such Confidential Information
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives (including advisers, auditors and insurers) and Group members on a need-to-know basis is permitted, with the Receiving Party liable for them.

findings.quote: to the minimum extent required by an order of any court of competent jurisdiction
findings.why: Disclosure is permitted where required by law, regulator, court or stock exchange, and notice and cooperation are qualified by legal permission and at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Return or destruction within ten Business Days with officer-signed confirmation matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: copies of any Confidential Information that are securely stored in routine, automated electronic backup or archiving systems
findings.why: Retention in automated backups and legally required copies is allowed and clause 6.3 keeps retained copies confidential.

findings.quote: other than the limited right to use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted other than use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: save that nothing in this Agreement shall exclude or limit either Party's liability for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation
findings.why: The as-is basis, mutual no-warranty and no-reliance wording are retained with the fraud carve-out intact, and clause 7.5 includes no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party, except as required by law
findings.why: A mutual restriction on announcements without prior written consent, except as required by law, is retained.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement
findings.why: Only business contact details are expected and any other personal data requires a separate DPA first; the added EU GDPR and French law references in 1.1.3 only widen the legislation covered.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: A two-year term with 30 days' notice and three years' survival (10.3) with Trade Secrets protected while they remain secret matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Equitable relief is mutual and expressed as 'entitled to seek', and clause 11.2 keeps remedies cumulative.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: Neither Party may assign or deal with its rights without the other's prior written consent.

findings.quote: our group policy is to request French law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Commercial Court of Lyon
findings.why: The margin comment requests French law and exclusive Lyon jurisdiction, or Swiss law as a fallback, while the text still reads England and Wales law and courts (12.10 and 12.11); this is a change-of-governing-law request that must be declined or escalated.
findings.draft_redline: Retain clauses 12.10 and 12.11 unchanged; if a concession is needed, offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to agree to French or Swiss law or jurisdiction, as Halyard's standard is English law, but we would be happy to discuss English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction.
